method_card.title: Food, Drink and Meals
method_card.content:
This lesson covers food and drink vocabulary, partitive articles, and describing mealtimes.

FrenchEnglish
le painbread
le fromagecheese
le poissonfish
le pouletchicken
la viandemeat
les légumesvegetables
les fruitsfruit
la glaceice cream
le gâteaucake
l'eau (f)water
le jus d'orangeorange juice
le petit déjeunerbreakfast
le déjeunerlunch
le dînerdinner
végétarien(ne)vegetarian

Partitive articles express 'some' or 'any' with food and drink: du (masculine singular) = du pain; de la (feminine singular) = de la viande; de l' (before a vowel) = de l'eau; des (plural) = des légumes. After a negative, all partitives become de (or d' before a vowel): Je ne mange pas de viande. Je ne bois pas d'alcool.

Model: Au petit déjeuner, je mange du pain et je bois du jus d'orange. Au déjeuner, je prends du poulet avec des légumes. Je ne mange pas de glace parce que c'est trop sucré. — For breakfast, I eat bread and drink orange juice. For lunch, I have chicken with vegetables. I don't eat ice cream because it is too sweet.
steps: Learn the key food and drink vocabulary with their genders
Master partitive articles (du, de la, de l', des) for unspecified amounts
Remember that partitives always become de/d' after a negative
Practice describing what you eat and drink at each mealtime

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — partitive articles are a high-frequency grammar test point

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Je mange du pain et du fromage.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Je mange = I eat. du pain = (some) bread. du fromage = (some) cheese.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: du is the partitive article for masculine nouns — both pain and fromage are masculine.

worked_examples.question: How do partitive articles change after a negative?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: In positive sentences, use: du (m), de la (f), de l' (vowel), des (pl).

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: After ne…pas, ALL partitives become de (or d' before a vowel).

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Example: Je mange du poisson → Je ne mange pas de poisson.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: After a negative, du / de la / de l' / des all become de (or d' before a vowel).

bronze.question: Match the French food vocabulary to the English meaning
Match the French drinks and mealtimes to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct partitive article

gaps.correct_explain: du is the partitive for masculine singular nouns. Le pain is masculine → du pain.

wrong.des: des is for plural nouns. Pain is singular masculine — use du.
wrong.de la: de la is for feminine nouns. Pain is masculine — use du.

gaps.correct_explain: de la is the partitive for feminine singular nouns. La viande is feminine → de la viande.

wrong.du: du is for masculine nouns. Viande is feminine — use de la.

gaps.correct_explain: des is the partitive for plural nouns. Les légumes is plural → des légumes.

wrong.du: du is for singular masculine nouns. Légumes is plural — use des.

bronze.question: Complete the negative sentence about food

gaps.correct_explain: After a negative, the partitive becomes de. Je ne mange pas de viande.

wrong.du: After a negative, du changes to just de.
wrong.de la: After a negative, de la changes to just de.

gaps.correct_explain: After a negative and before a vowel, the partitive becomes d'. Je ne bois pas d'alcool.

wrong.de l': After a negative, de l' becomes just d'. Je ne bois pas d'alcool.

bronze.question: What does 'Au petit déjeuner, je mange des céréales et je bois du jus d'orange' mean?
options: For breakfast, I eat cereal and drink orange juice
For lunch, I eat cereal and drink orange juice
For breakfast, I eat bread and drink milk
For dinner, I eat cereal and drink coffee

bronze.question: Which partitive article completes the sentence: 'Elle boit ___ eau'?

bronze.source_text: Mon plat préféré, c'est le poulet rôti. Je ne mange pas de viande rouge.
model_answers: My favourite dish is roast chicken. I don't eat red meat.
hints: mon plat préféré = my favourite dish

silver.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct partitive article
silver.english: For lunch, I have some fish and some fresh vegetables.

gaps.correct_explain: du is correct because poisson is masculine singular.

wrong.de: de is only used after a negative. This is a positive sentence — use du.
wrong.de la: de la is for feminine nouns. Poisson is masculine — use du.
de la is feminine singular. Légumes is plural — use des.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Je ne mange pas du poisson parce que je suis végétarienne.
silver.explanation: After ne…pas, the partitive du must change to de: Je ne mange pas de poisson.
silver.translation: I don't eat fish because I am vegetarian.

silver.question: Build the sentence in French
silver.english: I eat bread and cheese for breakfast.

distractor_labels.de la: wrong gender — pain and fromage are both masculine, so use du not de la

silver.source_text: For dinner, I eat meat and vegetables. I drink water.
model_answers: Au dîner, je mange de la viande et des légumes. Je bois de l'eau.

gold.question: Build the sentence in French
gold.english: Some people become vegetarian to improve their diet.

distractor_labels.devient: wrong conjugation — certains is plural (ils), needs deviennent not devient
distractor_labels.végétarien: wrong number — certains is plural, the adjective must agree: végétariens
distractor_labels.son: wrong possessive — leur (their) not son (his/her) because the subject is plural (certains)

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a restaurant in France and the waiter comes to take your order.

bullets.prompt: Ask politely to see the menu.
bullets.model_answer: Bonjour ! Est-ce que je pourrais voir la carte, s'il vous plaît ?
bullets.note: je pourrais (conditional = polite) + la carte (the menu — not le menu)

bullets.prompt: Order a main course and a drink.
bullets.model_answer: Je voudrais du poulet avec des légumes, s'il vous plaît. Et comme boisson, je vais prendre de l'eau.
bullets.note: je voudrais (polite conditional) + partitive articles (du / des / de l') + comme boisson

bullets.prompt: Give your opinion on the food.
bullets.model_answer: C'était délicieux ! J'ai adoré le poulet — il était très bon.
bullets.note: c'était (imperfect for description), j'ai adoré (passé composé), il était (imperfect)
l'addition = the bill; this is a set phrase

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: Mon régime comprend des fruits, des légumes frais, du poisson et du poulet. Je ne mange pas de glace car c'est trop sucré.
gold.correct_text: Mon régime comprend des fruits, des légumes frais, du poisson et du poulet. Je ne mange pas de glace car c'est trop sucré.
gold.translation: My diet includes fruit, fresh vegetables, fish and chicken. I don't eat ice cream because it's too sweet.

gold.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct word
gold.english: I would like some water and the menu, please.

gaps.correct_explain: voudrais is the conditional of vouloir, used for polite requests: je voudrais = I would like.

wrong.vais: vais expresses near future (I am going to) — different meaning. For a polite request, use the conditional: voudrais.
wrong.veux: veux is present tense (I want) — less polite. In formal settings, use the conditional: voudrais.

gaps.correct_explain: carte means menu (list of dishes). La carte = the menu.

wrong.menu: menu in French refers to a set meal (prix fixe), not the general list of dishes. The menu is la carte.
